facts.fact: The successful Create.Opened response contains the one-bit DisableCache field alongside granted access, contexts and file information. It is a low-level response field, not itself an authorization, quota or section-denial contract.

FO_CACHE_SUPPORTED is enabled only with infinite FileInfoTimeout, without FILE_NO_INTERMEDIATE_BUFFERING, and with DisableCache unset. SectionObjectPointer is assigned separately before this condition. Thus setting the bit prevents this open from gaining that cache-supported flag; it does not establish section creation rejection.

FastIoWrite refuses the cached fast path without FO_CACHE_SUPPORTED. Ordinary writes select the noncached implementation when that flag is absent or paging/noncache flags apply. Cached extending writes request new EOF through SetInformation before proceeding. These are routing facts, not proof that all mappings, dirty-page storage or kernel allocations are bounded by user-mode callbacks.

The source accounts for user-writable sections with no open handles. Default cleanup semantics permit mapped I/O to deleted files after Cleanup. FlushAndPurgeOnCleanup changes those semantics and may discard cached data; it is not an established universal mapping-denial or safe-drain substitute. Namespace removal and handle cleanup cannot alone authorize releasing orphan storage charges.

OperationContext exposes the current request/response; SetOperation replaces a low-level operation. The process-ID helper is explicitly limited to Create/Open and qualifying Rename requests, returning zero for other kinds. It is not a universal Write/Close caller identity or an outside-writer exclusion mechanism.

The normal Create/Open wrappers populate contexts, access and file information without an explicit DisableCache assignment in the inspected successful branches. A candidate must explicitly freeze where the response bit is set, covering every successful Create disposition/Open path. Cleanup and Close callbacks use retained file contexts; Cleanup cannot report a callback failure through its void interface.

The driver registers section-creation, modified-page-write and cache-flush/lazy-write callbacks independently of its FastIoWrite dispatch. Their registration reinforces that a cached-write flag condition cannot substitute for tracing the section and paging lifecycle implementations.

supported_candidate_topology: An explicitly pinned low-level Create operation wrapper can call the original operation and set DisableCache on every successful Opened response, with source-frozen success/reparse/error rules. This is a candidate design inference, not an implemented adapter or runtime proof.

The quota adapter still needs synchronized live/pending/orphan allocation, node, context and request reservations across all mutation paths, retaining ownership through deferred work and final release.

Opening identity and rights may be bound to a retained per-open context, but transferred handles, section references, subsequent callers and outside writers require a separate supported confinement contract.

facts.fact: Section acquisition is a void callback taking the node's exclusive Full lock and setting its CreateSection TLS flag. Release clears the flag and releases that lock. Modified-page acquisition tries that lock and returns success or STATUS_CANT_WAIT; flush/lazy-write callbacks also manage locks and thread/top-level bookkeeping. None of these inspected bodies dispatches a user-mode mapping-authorization request or implements a universal mapping refusal.

facts.locations: DriverEntry fast-I/O and CacheManager callback registration
facts.fact: The registered section acquire/release, modified-write, flush and lazy-write callbacks are the functions in callbacks.c. This resolves the previous guessed fastio.c implementation-path gap, without turning cache routing into mapping denial.

Header callback declarations and the CreateSection/LazyWriteThread/CcFlush node bookkeeping agree with the inspected implementations. These are synchronization state, not retained originating-process authorization for each mapped/paging write.

Microsoft documents that filters cannot fail SyncTypeOther. For SyncTypeCreateSection it describes failure with STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES when memory is insufficient. This reference does not support proposing a generic STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED minifilter shortcut for mapping authorization. It concerns the FSFilter interface, which must not be conflated with WinFsp's void FastIo callback.

eq083-winfsp-section-source-reviewer-rep.conclusion: DisableCache remains an open-specific cache-routing control. The newly traced callbacks provide section/cache synchronization rather than an authorization denial mechanism. A quota design must retain reservations through mapping, paging, deferred work and final release unless a separately supported enforceable exclusion policy is established.
